claim_reference: Adv. Funct. Mater. 2026, 36:e75639, Figures 2f, 2g, 3e, S6, S7 (Cell Phenotype Statistics & Pseudoreplication)

preregistration.hypothesis: Cell biology significance claims (p < 0.001, p < 0.01) reported in Figures 2 and 3 remain statistically valid when modeled with hierarchical mixed-effects models accounting for clustering within N=3 biological hydrogel replicates.
preregistration.primary_metric: Type I error rate under ICC in [0.05, 0.35] and cluster-adjusted p-values for cell spreading / morphology assays.
preregistration.decision_rule: SUPPORTED if Type I error rate remains <= 7.5% and cluster-adjusted p-values remain < 0.05; WEAKENED if Type I error rate inflates >= 20% or cluster-adjusted p-values exceed 0.05; CONTRADICTED if biological replicate variance accounts for >50% of total variance.

summary: Biostatistical audit reveals severe nested pseudoreplication across Figures 2f, 2g, 3e, S6, and S7. The authors pooled N=32--240 individual cells across N=3 hydrogel replicates as independent observations. Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that with realistic biological clustering (ICC = 0.10--0.20), the true False Positive Rate inflates from 5% to 36.3%--54.7%. True degrees of freedom shrink from df=238 to df=4, jumping the t-critical threshold by 40.9% and substantially inflating nominal p-values under cluster-robust hierarchical modeling.
